name: Kolumbo hydrothermal field

sources.title: Wikipedia — Kolumbo (crater 1.5 km wide, floor at about 500 m; the 1650 eruption)
Kilias et al. 2013, Scientific Reports — New insights into hydrothermal vent processes in the unique shallow-submarine arc-volcano, Kolumbo
NOAA Ocean Explorer — Hydrothermal vents in the Kolumbo crater

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1513696_kolumbo.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/placekit.py) with AI assistance. On the floor of Kolumbo's crater, about 500 m down, 7 km north-east of Santorini: the central part of the hydrothermal field, some 200 m across — low mounds of vent deposits, sulphide chimneys up to 4-6 m high (the tallest, «Poet's Candle», about 6 m), rusty orange where they have oxidised, on grey and orange iron-stained sediment. The place and height of each chimney are approximate. No marine life in the model (the bacterial mats are Offlined's to draw).
